title: Double Gaussian phase integral
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$ on $\mathbb R^n$. For every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the iterated integral over independent standard Gaussian vectors $t,y\in\mathbb R^n$ of $e^{ia\langle t,x\rangle}e^{ib\langle y,t\rangle}f(y)$ equals, as a complex number, the real integral $\int f(y)\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(a x_i+b y_i)^2\right)\,d\gamma(y)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure
